definition_zh: n. 大错；失误；vi. 犯大错；跌跌撞撞地走；盲动
definition_en: a careless or stupid mistake, or to move clumsily without seeing
core_image: 黑夜里在房间里乱撞踢翻椅子的人
scene: 他深夜摸黑走进客厅，撞翻了茶几上的花瓶。The general's blunder cost the army the whole campaign.
sceneCN: 这里 blunder 是名词「大错」（第 1 个义项：因粗心或愚钝而犯的重大失误）；句意是将军的一次重大失误葬送了整场战役。

derivatives.zh: blunder 加 -er，义为「屡犯大错的人」
blunder 加 -ing，义为「笨拙而多失误的」

senses.title: A serious careless mistake
senses.definition: a big mistake made through carelessness or stupidity
senses.definitionCN: 因粗心或愚钝而犯的重大错误
senses.example: The general's blunder cost the army the whole campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 将军的一次重大失误葬送了整场战役。
senses.why: The verb first meant to stumble blindly; a blunder is a moral stumble.
senses.whyCN: 动词本义是「盲目跌撞」，blunder 便是道德上的跌撞。

senses.title: A diplomatic or tactical error
senses.definition: an error in policy, negotiation, or strategy with wide consequences
senses.definitionCN: 政策、谈判或战略上后果严重的失误
senses.example: The treaty turned out to be a historic blunder.
senses.exampleCN: 这份条约被证明是历史性的失策。
senses.why: States stumble as people do, only on a larger floor.
senses.whyCN: 国家如人一样会跌倒，只是跌在更大的地板上。

senses.title: To move blindly and clumsily
senses.definition: to walk or grope clumsily without seeing where one is going
senses.definitionCN: 在看不见的情况下笨拙摸索前行
senses.example: They blundered through the fog toward the lights.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在浓雾中跌跌撞撞地向灯光走去。
senses.why: The original sense: stumbling in the dark, literally.
senses.whyCN: 本义即在黑暗中跌撞前行，是字面用法。

senses.title: To enter or become involved by accident
senses.definition: to get into a situation carelessly or by mistake
senses.definitionCN: 因粗心或错误而卷入某处境
senses.example: He blundered into an argument not meant for him.
senses.exampleCN: 他误打误撞地卷入了一场与己无关的争执。
senses.why: Walking blindly, one crosses doors one never chose.
senses.whyCN: 盲目行走之人，难免误入未曾选择的门。

senses.title: To say the wrong thing
senses.definition: to make an embarrassing remark by mistake
senses.definitionCN: 无意间说出令人难堪的话
senses.example: She blundered by mentioning his lost job.
senses.exampleCN: 她失言提起了他丢工作的事。
senses.why: Speech, too, has dark rooms; talk blindly and you hit the furniture.
senses.whyCN: 言语也有暗室，盲目开口便会撞上家具。

senses.title: A chess mistake losing material
senses.definition: in chess, a move that loses material or the game
senses.definitionCN: 国际象棋中损失子力或致败的错着
senses.example: A last-minute blunder gave his opponent the win.
senses.exampleCN: 最后时刻的一步大漏着让对手取胜。
senses.why: Chess adopted the word for the move a blind man might make.
senses.whyCN: 棋界借该词形容只有盲者才会走出的错着。

senses.title: To proceed stupidly despite warnings
senses.definition: to continue in error even with the danger visible
senses.definitionCN: 尽管危险明显仍继续犯错
senses.example: The council blundered ahead with the road plan.
senses.exampleCN: 议会不顾一切地推进道路计划。
senses.why: Refusing to look is itself the blindness the word names.
senses.whyCN: 拒绝去看，正是该词所指的那种「盲」。

senses.title: To grope one's way to success by luck
senses.definition: to succeed only by luck rather than judgment
senses.definitionCN: 靠运气而非判断取得成功
senses.example: The detectives blundered onto the truth at last.
senses.exampleCN: 侦探们最终误打误撞地发现了真相。
senses.why: Even blind walkers sometimes find the right door.
senses.whyCN: 盲行者偶尔也会撞对门。

intro.en: Blunder probably comes from Old Norse blunda, to shut the eyes or doze.
intro.cn: blunder 一般认为出自古诺斯语 blunda「闭眼、打盹」。

items.en: a root of drowsy, blinking dark; related forms are Scandinavian.
items.cn: 词根与「昏睡、眨眼、昏暗」相关，同族词见于斯堪的纳维亚。

items.en: blunda meant to shut the eyes, doze; blundra meant to shut one's eyes to danger.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 blunda 意为「闭眼、打盹」，blundra 意为「对危险视而不见」。

items.en: blunder first meant to stumble about blindly, then to act blindly.
items.cn: 16 世纪英格兰北部用语中，blunder 先指盲目跌撞，后指盲目行事。

items.en: the mistake sense became dominant in general and military English.
items.cn: 17 至 18 世纪，「失误」义在通用语与军事用语中占主导。

items.en: now standard for any grave careless error, including in chess.
items.cn: 今为标准词，泛指一切重大疏失，包括棋类术语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the blund- sound; the near-meaning group gathers mistake words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 blund- 音；近义组收错误类词。

definition_zh: adj. 钝的，不锋利的；直率的，不客气的；v. 使变钝；减弱
definition_en: not sharp; saying things plainly without trying to be polite; to make an edge or a feeling less sharp
core_image: 一把用了整个冬天的刀，切个番茄都要压着使劲
scene: 刀用了一整个冬天，切番茄都得用力。The knife had gone blunt, and even a tomato took effort.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：blunt 指刀刃不锋利；句意是刀钝到切番茄都要费劲。

senses.title: Not sharp
senses.definition: having an edge or point that does not cut well
senses.definitionCN: 刃口或尖端不利、难以切割
senses.example: A blunt saw tears the wood instead of cutting it.
senses.exampleCN: 钝锯不是在锯木头，而是在撕木头。
senses.why: The word probably began as a description of a dull edge, and everything else grew from that.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初很可能只是描述钝刃，其余义项都由此生长。

senses.title: Saying things plainly
senses.definition: expressing an opinion plainly, even if it offends
senses.definitionCN: 直白表达看法，即使冒犯他人
senses.example: To be blunt, the plan will not work.
senses.exampleCN: 直说吧，这个方案行不通。
senses.why: A dull blade does not glide politely through the grain; blunt speech does not smooth its way either.
senses.whyCN: 钝刃不会顺纹滑过，直话也不会一路铺平。

senses.title: To make less sharp or less strong
senses.definition: to take the edge off a blade, or to weaken the force of a feeling or effect
senses.definitionCN: 使刀刃变钝，或削弱情感与效果的力量
senses.example: Time had blunted the shock of the news.
senses.exampleCN: 时间已经削弱了这条消息带来的冲击。
senses.why: The physical sense of dulling an edge extends to dulling an emotion.
senses.whyCN: 「把刃弄钝」的实体义延伸到「把情绪磨钝」。

intro.en: Blunt appears in English in the fourteenth century; its deeper origin is uncertain, though a Scandinavian source is often suggested.
intro.cn: blunt 在十四世纪出现于英语；更深来源不确定，常有斯堪的纳维亚来源之说。

items.en: The word is first recorded in Middle English for a dull edge.
items.cn: 这个词最早以「钝刃」义见于中古英语。

items.en: No source has been proved; Scandinavian forms are suggested.
items.cn: 来源未获证实，有人提出斯堪的纳维亚语形式。

items.en: The sense of rough or unpolished speech appears.
items.cn: 「言语粗直」这一义项出现。

items.en: Blunt becomes a verb meaning to dull an edge.
items.cn: blunt 转为动词，意为使刃变钝。

items.en: It extends to blunting pain, shock and appetite.
items.cn: 该词扩展到「减弱痛感、震惊与食欲」。

items.en: Both the knife sense and the speech sense are everyday.
items.cn: 刀义与言语义都是日常用法。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the bl- plus n or t shape; the near-meaning group splits between a dull edge and plain speech.
note.cn: 形近组保留 bl- 加 n 或 t 的形状；近义组分成「钝刃」与「直话」两支。

senses.title: Praising oneself too much

definition_en: to support or strengthen something, or a long cushion used as a prop
core_image: 一根木柱斜撑在将倒的墙边，墙面因此重新立直
scene: 球队连败之后，教练公开肯定队员的努力，士气才慢慢回来。The new evidence bolstered the prosecution's case.
sceneCN: 这里 bolster 指为论证增加支撑、使其更有力（第 5 个义项：加强论证）；句意为新证据加强了控方的论证。

senses.title: Support something already there
senses.definition: to support or reinforce something that is already present but weak
senses.definitionCN: 支撑或加固已经存在但脆弱的东西
senses.example: Extra beams were added to bolster the old roof.
senses.exampleCN: 又加了几根梁来加固旧屋顶。
senses.why: A bolster is a cushion placed under something to hold it up, so the verb begins as a physical prop.
senses.whyCN: bolster 本是一种塞在下面托住东西的垫枕，因此动词最初是物理支撑。

senses.title: Raise confidence
senses.definition: to improve someone's confidence or sense of security
senses.definitionCN: 提高某人的信心或安全感
senses.example: The coach's praise bolstered the young players.
senses.exampleCN: 教练的赞扬增强了年轻球员的信心。
senses.why: Confidence is a structure that can sag; support under it keeps the structure standing.
senses.whyCN: 信心是一种会下垂的结构；在下面加支撑就能让它立住。

senses.title: A long cushion
senses.definition: a long, firm cushion used on a bed or sofa
senses.definitionCN: 床或沙发上使用的长而硬的垫枕
senses.example: She placed a bolster behind her back.
senses.exampleCN: 她在背后放了一个长枕。
senses.why: The noun is the object that gave the verb its image: a cushion shaped to hold a body or a wall in place.
senses.whyCN: 名词是给动词提供意象的物件：一个形状适合托住身体或墙面的垫子。

senses.title: Prop something up physically
senses.definition: to raise or hold something with a support underneath
senses.definitionCN: 用下方的支撑把某物垫高或托住
senses.example: He bolstered the crate with two blocks of wood.
senses.exampleCN: 他用两块木头垫住了木箱。
senses.why: This is the concrete ancestor of every figurative use: a thing is placed under another thing so it cannot fall.
senses.whyCN: 这是所有比喻用法具体的前身：把一物置于另一物之下，使它不会倒下。

senses.title: Strengthen an argument
senses.definition: to add evidence or force to a claim or case
senses.definitionCN: 为某项主张或论证增加证据与力度
senses.example: The new evidence bolstered the prosecution's case.
senses.exampleCN: 新证据加强了控方的论证。
senses.why: A case is a structure of reasons; each new piece of evidence is a beam under it.
senses.whyCN: 论证是由理由构成的结构；每一份新证据都是它下面的一根梁。

senses.title: Shore up a market or currency
senses.definition: to intervene to keep a market, price or currency from falling
senses.definitionCN: 通过干预防止市场、价格或货币下跌
senses.example: The central bank bolstered the currency with reserves.
senses.exampleCN: 中央银行用储备支撑本国货币。
senses.why: A falling price is a wall leaning over; intervention puts a prop under it before it collapses.
senses.whyCN: 下跌的价格是一堵倾斜的墙；干预在它倒塌之前塞进一根支柱。

senses.title: Reinforce a defense
senses.definition: to strengthen a defensive position or force
senses.definitionCN: 加强防御阵地或防御力量
senses.example: Troops were sent to bolster the northern defenses.
senses.exampleCN: 部队被派去加固北部防线。
senses.why: Defense is literally a wall, so the oldest meaning of the word returns without any metaphor at all.
senses.whyCN: 防御字面上就是一堵墙，于是这个词最古老的含义无需任何比喻就回来了。

senses.title: Act as a support against pressure
senses.definition: to serve as the thing that keeps another from giving way
senses.definitionCN: 充当使另一物不致屈服的东西
senses.example: Allies bolstered the small state against pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 盟国支撑这个小国抵御压力。
senses.why: The word can describe the prop rather than the act of propping: to be the support is also to bolster.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以描述支撑物而非支撑动作：成为支撑也就是 bolster。

intro.en: Bolster began as the name of a long cushion, and the verb grew from the cushion's job of holding things up.
intro.cn: bolster 最初是一种长枕的名称，动词由垫枕「托住东西」的功能发展而来。

items.en: The noun is old in English; the figurative verb 'to support' appears by the 16c. and is now the dominant use.
items.cn: 这个名词在英语中很古老；比喻性的动词「支持」到十六世纪出现，如今已是主要用法。

items.en: Old English bolster named a cushion or pillow, especially one stuffed with hair or straw.
items.cn: 古英语 bolster 指垫枕，尤指填有毛发或稻草的枕头。

items.en: The word belongs to a Germanic family connected with swelling and stuffing, the idea of a bag filled out to hold weight.
items.cn: 这个词属于一个日耳曼词族，与「鼓起、填塞」有关，即一个被填满以承重的袋子。

items.en: Middle English kept the noun for bed cushions and began using it for any prop placed under a heavy object.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了这个表示床枕的名词，并开始用它指垫在重物下方的任何支撑物。

items.en: From roofs and crates the verb moved to confidence, evidence, markets and defenses, wherever a structure might sag.
items.cn: 从屋顶与木箱出发，这个动词转向信心、证据、市场与防御，凡是结构可能下垂之处都可使用。

note.en: The look-alike group shares spelling or the cushion root; the near-meaning group names ways of holding something up.
note.cn: 形近组共享拼写或「垫枕」词根；近义组列出托住某物的各种方式。

entries.definition: supported or strengthened in the past.
entries.definitionCN: 过去得到支撑或加强的。

entries.definition: the act of supporting or strengthening.
a case for carrying a handgun, unrelated in meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 携带手枪的皮套，词义无关。

entries.definition: to fit furniture with cushions and covering.
to bear weight or keep something from falling.
to make a structure or force stronger.
to support with a projecting structure or with reasons.
entries.definitionCN: 用外撑结构或理由支撑。

entries.definition: to support something weak so it does not collapse.
entries.definitionCN: 支撑脆弱之物以免倒塌。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the cushion under the sagging wall.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把「垫在歪墙下的枕头」留住。

normal.en: A bolster is a cushion put under something; the verb is that cushion's job.
normal.cn: bolster 是垫在下面的枕头；动词就是枕头的工作。

normal.en: Picture a beam leaning against a wall that is about to fall.
normal.cn: 想象一根梁斜靠在即将倒塌的墙上。

normal.en: Confidence, evidence and markets are all walls that can lean.
normal.cn: 信心、证据与市场都是可能倾斜的墙。

normal.en: Say BOL-ster, with the stress on the cushion itself.
normal.cn: 读成 BOL-ster，重音落在「垫枕」上。

normal.en: Link it with upholster: both words hide a cushion inside.
normal.cn: 把它和 upholster 联系：两个词里都藏着一个垫子。

abstract.en: Every figurative use keeps the geometry of one thing placed under another.
abstract.cn: 每个比喻用法都保留「一物置于另一物之下」的几何关系。

abstract.en: Support must arrive before collapse, which is why the word suggests urgency.
abstract.cn: 支撑必须在倒塌之前到达，所以这个词带有紧迫感。

abstract.en: To be the prop is also to bolster, so allies and evidence can share the name.
abstract.cn: 成为支撑物也就是 bolster，因此盟友与证据可以共用这个词。

examples.en: The new evidence bolstered the prosecution's case.
examples.cn: 新证据加强了控方的论证。

examples.en: The central bank moved to bolster the currency.
examples.cn: 中央银行采取行动支撑本国货币。

examples.en: Extra beams were added to bolster the old roof.
examples.cn: 又加了几根梁来加固旧屋顶。

dict_mnemonic.text: bolster 本是「长枕」：把枕头垫在要倒的东西下面，就是「支撑、加强」。

root: 古英语 bolster（垫枕），属日耳曼语族，与「填塞、鼓起」有关

sensesIntro.en: Bolster always places support under something; the senses differ in whether the thing supported is a roof, a currency, a case, a defense or a person's confidence.
sensesIntro.cn: bolster 始终是在某物下方加支撑；各义项的差别在于被支撑的是屋顶、货币、论证、防御还是人的信心。

core.en: A PROP UNDER A SAGGING STRUCTURE
core.cn: 倾斜结构下的一根支柱

branches.en: The literal act of holding something up.
branches.cn: 把某物托住的字面动作。

branches.en: Confidence and allies that keep a person or state from giving way.
branches.cn: 使个人或国家不致屈服的信心与盟友。

branches.en: The cushion that gave the word its shape.
branches.cn: 赋予这个词形状的垫枕。

branches.en: Evidence placed under a legal case.
branches.cn: 垫在法律论证下的证据。

branches.en: Markets and defenses that must not be allowed to fall.
branches.cn: 不容许倒下的市场与防御。

intro.en: The word is native English, and its parts are historical rather than productive.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语本族词，其构件是历史性的，而非能产的。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source here; the Germanic family shows the cushion image directly.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语来源；日耳曼词族直接展示「垫枕」意象。

items.meaning: a cushion used as a prop
items.example: A bolster held the beam in place.
He was the quiet bolsterer of the plan.

items.exampleCN: 他们给旧椅子换了软垫。

items.example: They bolstered up the wall with props.

items.exampleCN: 新数据支持了这一主张。

definition_zh: 炸弹；轰炸；惨败
definition_en: a device that explodes and causes damage
core_image: 桥下被围起来的黑色装置
scene: 拆弹手小心地靠近桥下的那枚装置。The bomb was found under the bridge.
sceneCN: 这里 bomb 是「炸弹」（第 1 个义项：会爆炸并造成破坏的装置）；句意是桥下发现了一枚炸弹。

senses.title: An explosive device
senses.definition: a device that explodes and causes damage
senses.definitionCN: 会爆炸并造成破坏的装置
senses.example: The bomb was found under the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 桥下发现了一枚炸弹。
senses.why: This is the core sense, from a word for a booming sound.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心义项，来自表示轰响的词。

senses.title: To attack with bombs
senses.definition: to attack a place by dropping bombs on it
senses.definitionCN: 向某地投掷炸弹进行攻击
senses.example: Enemy planes bombed the port at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 敌机在黎明时轰炸了港口。
senses.why: The noun became a verb as soon as bombs were used in war.
senses.whyCN: 炸弹一用于战争，名词就变成了动词。

senses.title: To fail badly
senses.definition: to fail completely, as a play or a film might
senses.definitionCN: 彻底失败，如戏剧或电影票房惨淡
senses.example: The new play bombed with critics.
senses.exampleCN: 这出新戏被评论界批得很惨。
senses.why: A failure that goes down like an explosion kept the image of the bomb.
senses.whyCN: 像爆炸一样轰然倒下的失败，沿用炸弹的意象。

intro.en: Bomb goes back to a Latin word for a booming noise.
intro.cn: bomb 可上溯到拉丁语中表示轰响的词。

items.en: bombus meant a deep booming sound.
items.cn: bombus 指低沉的轰响。

items.en: bombe named an exploding shell.
items.cn: bombe 指会爆炸的炮弹。

items.en: bomb entered English as a word for a shell.
items.cn: bomb 以炮弹之义进入英语。

items.en: bombing from aircraft made the verb common.
items.cn: 飞机投弹使动词用法普及。

items.en: bomb also means to fail badly in slang.
items.cn: 在俚语中 bomb 也指惨败。

note.cn: 形近组与 bomb 押韵；近义组是其他爆炸物。

normal.en: A bomber is an aircraft or a person.
normal.cn: bomber 指轰炸机或投弹者。

normal.en: A bomb scare empties a building.
normal.cn: 炸弹恐吓会让整栋楼疏散。

abstract.en: See a dark object roped off on a bridge.
abstract.cn: 想象桥上被绳子围起来的黑色物体。

abstract.en: See a flash and a cloud of dust.
abstract.cn: 想象一道闪光与一团尘土。

abstract.cn: 想象一出烂戏之后空荡的剧场。

root: bomb 源自拉丁语 bombus（轰响），经法语 bombe 指爆炸的炮弹，进入英语后泛指炸弹，再引申为轰炸与惨败。

core.cn: 核心意象：桥下被围起来的黑色装置。

intro.en: Bomb takes -er and -ard to make related nouns and verbs.

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin; the items below share the idea of an explosion.

definition_zh: adj. （言辞）夸夸其谈的，浮夸空洞的
definition_en: of speech or writing, pompous and inflated, with grand words but little meaning
core_image: 讲台上的人声音越来越大，词句越来越空，句尾却没有落点
scene: 那场演讲满是宏大的词，散场后没人记得一句。The speech was bombastic, full of grand words that nobody could afterwards recall.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：bombastic 形容言辞浮夸空洞；句意是那场演讲满是大词，散场后无人记得。

forms.label: 形容词原级（无屈折变化）

senses.title: Pompous and inflated in speech
senses.definition: using high-sounding words that sound impressive but carry little substance
senses.definitionCN: 使用听来堂皇却少有实质的夸张词语
senses.example: The minister answered a simple question in bombastic terms.
senses.exampleCN: 部长用一个简单的问题，答出一串浮夸的辞令。
senses.why: Bombast was the cotton used to pad a garment, and padded speech is speech stuffed with air.
senses.whyCN: bombast 原指给衣服填塞的棉絮，而「填充的言辞」就是塞满空气的话。

senses.title: Overloaded in style
senses.definition: of writing, heavily ornamented and overblown rather than clear
senses.definitionCN: 文章装饰过重、夸张而缺乏清晰
senses.example: The essay is bombastic where it should be plain.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章在该朴素的地方反而堆砌。
senses.why: The padding metaphor moves from a stuffed coat to a sentence stuffed with ornament.
senses.whyCN: 「填塞」的比喻从塞满棉衣转到塞满装饰的句子。

intro.en: Bombastic comes from bombast, the cotton used to pad clothes, from Old French bombace and Latin bombax.
intro.cn: bombastic 来自 bombast（填衣用的棉絮），经古法语 bombace 上溯拉丁语 bombax。

items.en: Bombax is cotton or cotton wool.
items.cn: bombax 意为棉花、棉絮。

items.en: Bombace names the padding in a garment.
items.cn: bombace 指衣物的填充物。

items.en: English bombast means cotton stuffing for clothes.
items.cn: 英语 bombast 指填塞衣服的棉絮。

items.en: The word moves from stuffing cloth to stuffing words.
items.cn: 这个词由填衣转向填词。

items.en: The adjective appears for inflated, empty style.
items.cn: 形容词出现，指浮夸空洞的文风。

items.en: Bombastic is now applied to speeches and prose.
items.cn: 现代 bombastic 多用于演讲与文章。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the bomb- stem; the near-meaning group ranks inflated style from pompous to merely swollen.
note.cn: 形近组共享 bomb- 词干；近义组把浮夸风格从自命不凡排到单纯臃肿。

entries.definition: Using pompous and elaborate language.

normalIntro.en: Bombast was the cotton that padded a coat; bombastic speech is padded with wind.
normalIntro.cn: bombast 是填大衣的棉絮；bombastic 的话是用空气填起来的。

normal.en: Bombast first meant cotton padding.
normal.cn: bombast 最初指填塞用棉絮。

normal.en: Padding hides shape; padded words hide meaning.
normal.cn: 填充物遮住形体；注水的词遮住意思。

normal.en: Add -ic and the noun becomes the style.
normal.cn: 加 -ic，名词变成风格形容词。

normal.en: A bombastic speech gets louder and emptier.
normal.cn: 浮夸的演讲越来越响，也越来越空。

normal.en: If you cannot restate the sentence plainly, it may be bombastic.
normal.cn: 若说不出一句朴素的重述，它可能就很浮夸。

abstract.en: A coat worn with nothing inside it.
abstract.cn: 里面什么都没有的大衣。

abstract.en: Volume standing in for meaning.
abstract.cn: 用音量顶替意思。

abstract.en: Words stuffed like a cushion.
abstract.cn: 像靠垫一样被塞满的词语。

examples.en: His bombastic introduction mentioned no actual proposal.
examples.cn: 他浮夸的开场白里没有提出任何实际方案。

examples.en: Critics called the manifesto bombastic and vague.
examples.cn: 批评者称这份宣言浮夸而含糊。

examples.en: The letter is bombastic, but the figures inside are precise.
examples.cn: 这封信写得浮夸，里面的数字却很精确。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「表述必夸张」——一开口就要把话说得又大又满，正是浮夸。

root: bombast（填衣棉絮，16 世纪转指「注水的言辞」）+ -ic（形容词后缀）

sensesIntro.en: A stuffed coat and a stuffed sentence are the same object: plenty of material, no shape.
sensesIntro.cn: 塞满的大衣与塞满的句子是同一件东西：材料很多，形制全无。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a voice rising through grand words that never land
core.cn: 核心意象：声音在宏大的词里升上去，却始终没有落点

branches.en: A simple question given a long loud answer.
branches.cn: 简单问题得到又长又响的回答。

branches.en: Applause after a sentence with no content.
An essay ornamented at every clause.
branches.cn: 每个分句都加了装饰的文章。

branches.en: A report that says little at length.
branches.cn: 说得很长、内容很少的报告。

branches.en: Padding standing where substance should be.
branches.cn: 该有实质之处塞满了填絮。

intro.en: Bombastic is a noun stem plus -ic; the list below builds the style words and the cotton root behind it.
intro.cn: bombastic 是名词词干加 -ic；下面列出风格词汇与背后的「棉」词根。

latinEntries.exampleCN: bombax 变成 bombast。
tumere 产生 tumid 与 tumour。

definition_zh: 纽带；联系；债券；结合
definition_en: a strong connection between people
core_image: 两个孩子牵着同一根绳子
scene: 两个孩子一起长大，之间有一种牢固的联结。A strong bond grew between the two children.
sceneCN: 这里 bond 是「纽带；联系」（第 1 个义项：人与人之间的情感连接）；句意是两个孩子之间形成了牢固的纽带。

senses.title: A close connection
senses.definition: a strong feeling that connects people
senses.definitionCN: 把人们连在一起的情感
senses.example: A strong bond grew between the two children.
senses.exampleCN: 两个孩子之间形成了牢固的纽带。
senses.why: This comes from the oldest sense of something that ties.
senses.whyCN: 这来自「系住」的最古老含义。

senses.title: A financial certificate
senses.definition: a document promising to repay money with interest
senses.definitionCN: 承诺连本带息偿还的凭证
senses.example: He bought a government bond for his savings.
senses.exampleCN: 他把积蓄买了政府债券。
senses.why: A bond ties the lender and the borrower until the money is repaid.
senses.whyCN: 债券把出借人与借款人系在一起，直到还清为止。

senses.title: To join firmly
senses.definition: to stick things together very strongly
senses.definitionCN: 把物体牢牢粘合在一起
senses.example: The glue bonds wood to metal.
senses.exampleCN: 这种胶能把木头粘到金属上。
senses.why: The verb keeps the physical image of tying two things into one.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了把两物系成一体的具体意象。

intro.en: Bond comes from an Old Norse word for something that ties.
intro.cn: bond 来自古诺尔斯语中表示「系住之物」的词。

items.en: band meant a thing that ties or binds.
items.cn: band 指用来系或捆的东西。

items.en: bond named a rope, a chain and a duty.
items.cn: bond 指绳索、锁链，也指义务。

items.en: a bond became a written promise to pay.
items.cn: bond 成为一种书面的付款承诺。

items.en: chemists spoke of the bond between atoms.

items.en: bond covers feelings, money and glue.
items.cn: 如今 bond 兼指情感、债券与黏合。

note.cn: 形近组只差一个元音；近义组是表示联系与连接的词。

normal.en: A family bond holds people together.

examples.cn: 这种胶能把木头粘到金属上。

sensesIntro.en: A tie between people, a paper promise to pay, and the act of joining.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two children holding the same rope.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个孩子牵着同一根绳子。

intro.en: Bond takes -age and -holder to name a state and a person.

latinIntro.en: The base is Old Norse; the items below share the idea of tying.

definition_zh: n. 奴役，束缚；（对习惯、债务等的）受制
definition_en: the state of being a slave or of being tightly controlled; also a state of being held by a habit or debt
core_image: 一纸契约把一个人钉在田里，年复一年
scene: 契约把人拴了十年，债务还比契约活得更久。The contract held him in bondage for ten years, and the debt outlived it.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：bondage 指被奴役、被束缚的状态；句意是契约把他拴了十年，债务还比契约更久。

forms.label: 不可数名词（无屈折变化）

senses.title: The state of being a slave
senses.definition: the condition of being owned or forced to work without freedom
senses.definitionCN: 被占有或被迫无偿劳作的处境
senses.example: The law ended formal bondage but not the debt behind it.
senses.exampleCN: 法律终结了正式奴役，却没有终结其背后的债务。
senses.why: Bond first meant a serf, a person bound to the land, and -age names the condition.
senses.whyCN: bond 最初指被绑在土地上的农奴，-age 表示其状态。

senses.title: Being controlled by something
senses.definition: a state in which a habit, debt or feeling controls a person choices
senses.definitionCN: 习惯、债务或情感控制个人选择的状态
senses.example: He described his years of bondage to the bottle.
senses.exampleCN: 他讲述了自己被酒精控制的那几年。
senses.why: The legal sense loosens into any condition where a person cannot act freely.
senses.whyCN: 法律义松动为「一个人无法自由行动」的任何处境。

intro.en: Bondage is bond plus -age; bond first meant a peasant bound to the land.
intro.cn: bondage 是 bond 加 -age；bond 最初指被束缚于土地的农奴。

items.en: Bond means a householder or a tied peasant.
items.cn: bond 意为户主或被束缚的农人。

items.en: Bindan means to tie, the verb behind bond.
items.cn: bindan 意为捆绑，是 bond 背后的动词。

items.en: English bond names a serf or a binding tie.
items.cn: 英语 bond 指农奴或束缚性的纽带。

items.en: The suffix -age names the condition of the bound.
items.cn: 词尾 -age 表示被束缚者的处境。

items.en: The word is used in arguments against slavery.
items.cn: 废奴论争中使用了这个词。

items.en: Bondage also covers debt, habit and addiction.
items.cn: 现代也指债务、习惯与成瘾的束缚。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the bond- stem or the -age ending; the near-meaning group ranks loss of freedom from slavery to captivity.
note.cn: 形近组共享 bond- 词干或 -age 词尾；近义组把失去自由从奴役排到囚禁。

The forming of a close relationship.

entries.definition: The condition of being forced to serve.
The state of being kept prisoner.

entries.definitionCN: 被置于控制之下的状态。

normalIntro.en: Bond is a tie, and bondage is the tie that will not come off.
normalIntro.cn: bond 是束缚，bondage 就是解不下来的那种束缚。

normal.en: Bind means tie, and bond is the tie itself.
normal.cn: bind 意为捆绑，bond 就是那根绑定之物。

normal.en: -age makes a state, as in marriage.

normal.en: So bondage is the state of being tied.
normal.cn: 所以 bondage 是「被绑住」的状态。

normal.en: Bond once meant a peasant tied to the land.
normal.cn: bond 曾指被绑在土地上的农奴。

normal.en: Debt and habit can tie a person just as tightly.
normal.cn: 债务与习惯也能一样紧地绑住人。

abstract.en: A contract that holds a body.
abstract.cn: 攥住身体的契约。

abstract.en: A knot you did not tie yourself.
abstract.cn: 不是你亲手打的结。

abstract.en: Freedom lent out and never returned.
abstract.cn: 借出后再没归还的自由。

examples.en: The novel follows a family freed from bondage in the 1860s.
examples.cn: 这部小说写的是一个在一八六零年代摆脱奴役的家庭。

examples.en: Debt bondage still traps workers in some industries.
examples.cn: 债务奴役至今仍困住某些行业的工人。

examples.en: He spoke of his bondage to gambling without self-pity.
examples.cn: 他谈起自己被赌博束缚的岁月，没有自怜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「绑得紧」——被绑得太紧，动弹不得，就是奴役般的束缚。

root: bond（纽带、农奴）+ -age（状态、身份）

sensesIntro.en: A serf bound to land and a man bound to a bottle share one structure: a tie that decides what the person may do.
sensesIntro.cn: 被绑在土地上的农奴与被酒精绑住的人，结构相同：一根决定你还能做什么的绳。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a contract nailing a person to one field year after year
core.cn: 核心意象：一纸契约把一个人钉在一块田里，年复一年

branches.en: A worker who cannot leave the estate.
branches.cn: 无法离开庄园的劳作者。

intro.en: Bondage is a stem plus -age, a suffix that names states; the list below covers it and the vocabulary of tying and freedom.
intro.cn: bondage 是词干加 -age，这个后缀表示状态；下面列出它以及「捆绑与自由」词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin servus is a slave, vinculum is a bond, and liber is free.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 servus 意为奴隶，vinculum 意为锁链，liber 意为自由的。

latinEntries.exampleCN: servus 产生 servant 与 servitude。
vinculum 产生 vinculum 与 invincible。
liber 产生 liberty 与 liberal。

definition_zh: 奖金；额外的好处
definition_en: extra money paid to an employee as a reward
core_image: 年底发到手里的额外信封
scene: 年终公司给每个人发了一笔奖金。Everyone received a bonus at the end of the year.
sceneCN: 这里 bonus 是「奖金」（第 1 个义项：工资之外的额外报酬）；句意是年底每个人都拿到一笔奖金。

derivatives.zh: 语义关联词，义为奖金、赏金

senses.title: Extra pay for work
senses.definition: extra money added to normal pay as a reward
senses.definitionCN: 在正常工资之外额外支付的报酬
senses.example: Everyone received a bonus at the end of the year.
senses.exampleCN: 年底每个人都拿到一笔奖金。
senses.why: This is the main sense, from the Latin word for good.
senses.whyCN: 这是主要义项，来自拉丁语中表示「好」的词。

senses.title: Something extra and good
senses.definition: an unexpected advantage that comes with something
senses.definitionCN: 随某事物而来的意外好处
senses.example: Free breakfast was an added bonus.
senses.exampleCN: 免费早餐是个额外的好处。
senses.why: Anything good beyond what was promised is felt as a bonus.
senses.whyCN: 超出承诺的任何好事，都会被当成一份额外奖励。

intro.en: Bonus is Latin for good, and it entered English through the stock market.
intro.cn: bonus 在拉丁语中意为「好的」，经股票市场进入英语。

items.en: bonus meant good or honest.
items.cn: bonus 意为好的、诚实的。

items.en: London brokers called a extra payment a bonus.
items.cn: 伦敦经纪人把额外的付款称为 bonus。

items.en: bonus named a share of profit paid to workers.
items.cn: bonus 指发给工人的一份利润。

items.en: bonus spread to any extra benefit.
items.cn: bonus 扩展到任何额外的好处。

items.en: bonus means extra pay or an added advantage.
items.cn: 如今 bonus 指奖金或额外的好处。

note.en: The look-alike group starts with bon-; the near-meaning group names rewards and perks.
note.cn: 形近组都以 bon- 开头；近义组是奖励与福利。

entries.definition: not real or not genuine
attractive or pretty
something given for good work
an extra amount paid above the usual price
an extra benefit from a job

normalIntro.en: Bonus comes from the Latin word for good, so it is always something good added on.
normalIntro.cn: bonus 来自拉丁语中表示「好」的词，所以总是一份额外的好东西。

normal.en: The plural of bonus is bonuses.
normal.cn: bonus 的复数是 bonuses。

normal.en: An annual bonus comes once a year.
normal.cn: 年终奖金一年发一次。

normal.en: A bonus point is extra credit.
normal.cn: bonus point 指额外的加分。

normal.en: Free delivery is an added bonus.
normal.cn: 免费送货是一份额外好处。

normal.en: Bonanza means a sudden lucky gain.
normal.cn: bonanza 意为突然的好运与收获。

abstract.en: See an extra envelope at the end of December.
abstract.cn: 想象十二月底多出来的一个信封。

abstract.en: See a free gift inside a parcel.
abstract.cn: 想象包裹里附赠的小礼物。

abstract.en: See a score sheet with one extra point.
abstract.cn: 想象记分表上多加的一分。

examples.en: Everyone received a bonus at the end of the year.
examples.cn: 年底每个人都拿到一笔奖金。

examples.en: Free breakfast was an added bonus.
examples.cn: 免费早餐是个额外的好处。

examples.en: The bonus depends on how well the team performs.
examples.cn: 奖金取决于团队的表现。

dict_mnemonic.text: bon 在拉丁语里就是「好」，us 收尾像一枚盖章：好上加好，就是额外发的奖金。

root: bonus 是拉丁语中的「好」，十八世纪伦敦证券商借它指额外付款，十九世纪指分给工人的利润，后来泛指奖金与额外好处。

sensesIntro.en: Extra money for work, and any good thing added on.
sensesIntro.cn: 工资之外的额外报酬，以及任何附加的好处。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an extra envelope handed out in December.
core.cn: 核心意象：十二月多发的一个信封。

intro.en: Bonus is a whole Latin word; English builds few new forms from it.
intro.cn: bonus 本身是一个完整的拉丁词，英语由它构成的新词很少。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin; the items below share the idea of something good added.

definition_zh: 书；预订；账簿
definition_en: a set of printed pages fastened together inside a cover
core_image: 窗边翻开的旧书
scene: 她在窗边翻着一本旧书。She was reading an old book by the window.
sceneCN: 这里 book 是「书」（第 1 个义项：装订成册的读物）；句意是她在窗边读一本旧书。

senses.title: Printed pages bound together
senses.definition: a set of printed pages fastened inside a cover
senses.definitionCN: 装订在封面内的一叠印刷书页
senses.example: She was reading an old book by the window.
senses.exampleCN: 她在窗边读一本旧书。
senses.why: This is the central sense, from a word for writing tablets.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心义项，来自表示书写板的词。

senses.title: To reserve in advance
senses.definition: to arrange to have a seat or room kept for you
senses.definitionCN: 事先安排保留座位或房间
senses.example: We booked a table for eight o'clock.
senses.exampleCN: 我们订了八点的桌子。
senses.why: Your name is written into a book, so to book means to put down a reservation.
senses.whyCN: 名字被写进册子里，所以 to book 就是登记预订。

senses.title: Financial records
senses.definition: the written records of money a business receives and spends
senses.definitionCN: 企业收支的书面记录
senses.example: The accountant keeps the books for the shop.
senses.exampleCN: 会计为这家店记账。
senses.why: Accounts were once kept in bound books, and the name stayed.
senses.whyCN: 账目过去记在装订的册子里，名称沿用至今。

intro.en: Book is linked to beech, the wood once used for writing tablets.
intro.cn: book 与山毛榉有关，这种木头曾用来做书写板。

items.en: boc meant a beech tree and a written document.
items.cn: boc 指山毛榉，也指书面文件。

items.en: book named a bound set of written pages.
items.cn: book 指装订成册的书页。

items.en: books of account recorded money.
items.cn: 账簿用来记录金钱。

items.en: to book became to reserve a place.
items.cn: to book 变成预订座位的意思。

items.en: book covers reading, reserving and accounts.
items.cn: 如今 book 兼指书籍、预订与账目。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one letter; the near-meaning group names kinds of books.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个字母；近义组是各类书籍。

a curved piece of metal for hanging things
to turn your eyes towards something
a book, especially a large one
a long written story

normalIntro.en: Book is paper and cover, and it is also the act of writing your name down.
normalIntro.cn: book 既是纸与封面，也是把名字写进册子的动作。

normal.en: Book and books are singular and plural.
normal.cn: 单数是 book，复数是 books。

normal.en: Book a room before you travel.
normal.cn: 出行前先预订房间。

normal.en: A bookcase holds many books.
normal.cn: 书柜能放很多书。

normal.en: A booklet is a small thin book.
normal.cn: booklet 指薄薄的小册子。

normal.en: By the book means following the rules.
normal.cn: by the book 意为照章办事。

abstract.en: See an open book on a window sill.
abstract.cn: 想象窗台上摊开的一本书。

abstract.en: See rows of figures in an account book.
abstract.cn: 想象账簿里一行行的数字。

examples.cn: 她在窗边读一本旧书。

examples.cn: 我们订了八点的桌子。

examples.en: The accountant keeps the books for the shop.
examples.cn: 会计为这家店记账。

dict_mnemonic.text: book 里的 oo 像两本并排立着的书，两个圆圈就是书脊上的两道圆标。

root: book 源自古英语 boc，与山毛榉同源，古人用山毛榉木板写字，后指装订成册的书，又引申为账簿与预订。

sensesIntro.en: A bound set of pages, a reservation, and a record of money.
sensesIntro.cn: 装订成册的书、预订，以及金钱的记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open book on a window sill.
core.cn: 核心意象：窗台上摊开的一本书。

intro.cn: book 可与 case、let、shelf 构成复合词，也可加 -ing。

a book, especially a large one

definition_zh: n. 书立，书挡；v. 在两端夹住；以……开始并以……结束
definition_en: a support placed at the end of a row of books; also to stand at both ends of something or to begin and end with it
core_image: 两块木片把一排放歪的诗集夹得笔直
scene: 两块木片把一排放歪的诗集夹得笔直。Two wooden bookends held the row of poetry straight.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：bookend 指夹在书排两端的书立；句意是两块木片把一排放歪的诗集夹得笔直。

pos.zh: 在两端夹住；以……开始并结束

senses.title: An object at the end of a row of books
senses.definition: one of a pair of supports that keep a row of books upright
senses.definitionCN: 成对使用、让一排书保持直立不歪的支撑物
senses.example: A brass bookend shaped like a lion held up the atlas.
senses.exampleCN: 一只狮子造型的黄铜书立撑住了那本地图册。
senses.why: The compound simply names a prop placed at the end of books.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词直接命名了摆在书排末端的支撑物。

senses.title: To stand at both ends of something
senses.definition: to be placed at the two outer ends of a line or period
senses.definitionCN: 被安置在一排或一段时间的两个外侧端点
senses.example: Two tall towers bookend the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 两座高塔分立在桥的两端。
senses.why: The image of the shelf support widens to any pair of ends.
senses.whyCN: 书架支撑的意象扩大为任意一对端点。

senses.title: To begin and end with something
senses.definition: to open and close a series or event with the same element
senses.definitionCN: 用同一元素开启并收束一组事物或活动
senses.example: A slow ballad bookends the album.
senses.exampleCN: 一首慢歌为这张专辑开场并收尾。
senses.why: If two objects frame a row, they can frame a sequence of events too.
senses.whyCN: 既然两个物件能夹住一排东西，也就能框住一串事件。

intro.en: Bookend joins book, a bound volume, to end, the outer edge of a shelf.
intro.cn: bookend 由 book（装订成册的书）与 end（书架的外端）组合而成。

items.en: Boc means a book, once written on beechwood.
items.cn: boc 意为书，早先写在山毛榉木板上。

items.en: Book settles as the name for a bound volume.

items.en: Ende means an end, a boundary.

items.en: The compound names the prop at a shelf end.

items.en: Bookend extends to anything placed at two ends.

items.en: Publishers bookend a series with matching covers.
items.cn: 如今出版方用配套封面为一套书首尾呼应。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the book- stem; the near-meaning group ranks supports from the specific to the abstract.
note.cn: 形近组共享 book- 词干；近义组把支撑物从具体排到抽象。

entries.definition: A device that keeps something fixed.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物固定不动的装置。

normalIntro.en: A bookend is literally the end that holds the books.

normal.en: Book names the object it holds.
normal.cn: book 点明它夹住的是书。

normal.en: End names where it stands.
normal.cn: end 点明它所在的位置。

normal.en: So a bookend sits at the end of a row.
normal.cn: 所以 bookend 就是立在书排末端之物。

normal.en: Two of them squeeze a row into line.
normal.cn: 两个一起把一排书夹成一条线。

normal.en: Anything at both ends of a story bookends it.
normal.cn: 任何故事首尾两端的东西都能「夹住」它。

abstract.en: Two hands closing a row.
abstract.cn: 两只手合拢一排东西。

abstract.en: The frame of a straight line.
abstract.cn: 一条直线的边框。

abstract.en: A beginning and an end that agree.
abstract.cn: 彼此呼应的开头与结尾。

abstract.en: See a hand pushing a sales chart upward.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把销售曲线往上推。

abstract.en: See a rocket with an extra engine.
abstract.cn: 想象火箭上多绑了一台发动机。

abstract.en: See a child standing taller after praise.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子被表扬后挺直了腰。

examples.en: The new advert boosted sales by a third.
examples.cn: 新广告让销量提高了三分之一。

examples.en: Praise can boost a child's confidence.

dict_mnemonic.text: boot 是靴子，boost 多一个 s：脚往靴子里一蹬，人就往上抬，正合「提高、助推」的意思。

root: boost 词源不明，十九世纪出现在美国俚语中，本指从下面往上一推，后来引申为提高数量、促进发展与增强信心。

sensesIntro.en: A push that raises an amount, a help that lifts a mood, and a rise in confidence.
sensesIntro.cn: 把数量推高的力量、提振情绪的帮助，以及信心的上升。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pushing an upward arrow.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把向上的箭头推高。

intro.en: Boost takes -er and -ism to name a helper and an attitude.
intro.cn: boost 加 -er 与 -ism 可表示助推者与推崇的态度。

definition_zh: 靴子；汽车后备箱；启动（计算机）
definition_en: a strong shoe that covers the ankle and part of the leg
core_image: 门口沾满泥的一双靴子
scene: 门口放着一双沾满泥的靴子。A pair of muddy boots stood by the door.
sceneCN: 这里 boot 是「靴子」（第 1 个义项：包住脚踝和小腿的鞋）；句意是门口放着一双沾泥的靴子。

senses.title: A shoe that covers the ankle
senses.definition: a strong shoe covering the ankle and sometimes the leg
senses.definitionCN: 包住脚踝、有时包到小腿的结实鞋子
senses.example: A pair of muddy boots stood by the door.
senses.exampleCN: 门口放着一双沾泥的靴子。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, from a French word for a heavy shoe.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，来自法语中表示厚鞋的词。

senses.title: The luggage space of a car
senses.definition: the covered space at the back of a car for bags
senses.definitionCN: 汽车后部放行李的有盖空间
senses.example: Put the bags in the boot of the car.
senses.exampleCN: 把包放到汽车后备箱里。
senses.why: An old coach had a boot-shaped box for luggage at the back.
senses.whyCN: 旧式马车后部有个靴形的箱子放行李。

senses.title: To start a computer
senses.definition: to make a computer start working
senses.definitionCN: 让计算机开始运行
senses.example: The computer takes a minute to boot.
senses.exampleCN: 这台电脑启动需要一分钟。
senses.why: Starting a machine was compared to pulling yourself up by your bootstraps.
senses.whyCN: 启动机器被比作拉着自己的靴带站起来。

intro.en: Boot came from French, and its meaning spread from shoes to cars to computers.
intro.cn: boot 来自法语，意思从鞋子扩展到汽车，再到计算机。

items.en: bote meant a heavy shoe.
items.cn: bote 指厚重的鞋。

items.en: boot named leather footwear.
items.cn: boot 指皮革做的鞋靴。

items.en: boot named the luggage box on a coach.
items.cn: boot 指马车上的行李箱。

items.en: to boot became to start a computer.
items.cn: to boot 变成启动计算机。

items.en: boot covers footwear, car space and starting up.
items.cn: 如今 boot 兼指靴子、后备箱与启动。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one letter; the near-meaning group names shoes and luggage spaces.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个字母；近义组是鞋与行李空间。

normalIntro.en: Boot is a shoe that protects the leg, and a box that protects the bags.
normalIntro.cn: boot 是护住小腿的鞋，也是护住行李的箱子。

normal.en: Boot and boots are singular and plural.
normal.cn: 单数是 boot，复数是 boots。

normal.en: Put your boots by the door.
normal.cn: 把靴子放在门边。

normal.en: Bags go in the boot of a car.
normal.cn: 行李放在汽车后备箱里。

normal.en: To boot a computer is to start it.
normal.cn: 启动电脑就是让它开始运行。

normal.en: Reboot means to start again.
normal.cn: reboot 意为重新启动。

abstract.cn: 想象门口台阶上沾泥的靴子。

abstract.en: See a suitcase packed into a car boot.
abstract.cn: 想象行李箱被塞进后备箱。

abstract.en: See a screen lighting up at startup.
abstract.cn: 想象开机时亮起的屏幕。

root: boot 源自法语 bote（厚鞋），十四世纪指皮革靴，十七世纪指马车上的行李箱，二十世纪又用来表示计算机启动。
